title: Evaluate polyglot handshake patterns and prioritize binding-shim work for enterprise SDK ergonomics
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Synthesize customer requests about client binders across multiple languages and auth patterns, evaluate handshake/connection ergonomics for resumable streaming, and produce a prioritized list of candidate binding-shim implementations and API design recommendations for H1 engineering work. Focus is enterprise onboarding friction: multi-language examples, token rotation/refresh patterns, and clear streaming resume semantics that map to Redwood's routing/fallback model.
goals: Create a reproducible rubric to score client binding requests by enterprise impact, implementation effort, and security complexity
Deliver prioritized candidate designs (shim patterns + examples) for 3 community languages (Python, Java, Go) and one mobile runtime (iOS Swift)
Validate auth patterns for streaming and resumable sessions with Security/Trust & Safety and document recommended SDK primitives
Produce an implementation plan with clear handoffs to Eng, Design, and Docs teams for the top 2 shims
non_goals: Ship full SDK language bindings in this ticket
Replace existing official SDKs - this is focused on shim/adapter patterns and API ergonomics
Complete all enterprise legal/compliance negotiations (only flag requirements for Private deployments)
acceptance_criteria: Rubric published in Confluence with scoring examples and sample customer requests scored
Two candidate shim prototypes (one streaming-resume, one auth-rotation) implemented as PoC repos with README and minimal test harness
Security has signed off on recommended token rotation and refresh workflows for resumable streams
PM & Design approved UX patterns for connection handshake and error semantics
Prioritized backlog (top 2 shims) with engineering estimates and release signal (runtime-1.20 or console-2025.04)
proposed_rubric: CustomerSeverity (0-5): number of paying customers impacted and revenue risk
ImplementationEffort (0-5): estimated eng + infra dev time
SecurityComplexity (0-5): level of secrets/rotation and audit/logging required
InteropSurfaceArea (0-5): number of languages + platforms covered by a single shim
MaintenanceRisk (0-5): ongoing operational burden (backwards compat, spec drift)
customer_signals: Large fintech customer requests pattern for rotating OAuth tokens for long-lived streaming connections behind an enterprise gateway
Marketplace startup wants examples for resuming partially-consumed chat sessions across mobile and server SDKs
Platform team at a consumer app needs lightweight Go and Java bindings that mirror the hosted API's retry and fallback semantics
Several customers ask for official guidance on integrating their SSO with streaming sessions and automatic token refresh without rehydrating model state
representative_requests: "We have to keep our websocket streaming session alive across user token refreshes — how do we do that without losing KV cache state?" — Customer: Acme Finance
"Can you provide a minimal Swift example to resume a streaming response after a mobile network blip? We currently re-open the whole session and hit cold-start latency." — Customer: Nimbus Mobile
"We want a Java client that follows the same routing/fallback semantics as your REST SDK and falls back to a cheaper quantized model during burst limits." — Customer: DataBridge
tradeoffs_considered: Centralized shim maintained by Redwood vs. community-maintained adapters: trade-off between control and language coverage
Stateful resume APIs that keep KV cache in client vs. thin-client that replays prefix: trade-off between complexity and latency savings
Exposing token refresh primitives in official SDKs vs. recommending platform-specific integration: risk of encouraging insecure patterns if too prescriptive
recommended_next_steps: Run rubric against 15 recent enterprise requests and present scoring on 2025-03-07 triage meeting
Allocate 2 eng FTEs for 4 weeks for PoCs (Python streaming-resume and Java auth-rotation), assign design spike for UX flows
Schedule security deep-dive to finalize acceptable token rotation UX and required audit logs
Prepare docs template and example repo structure for shim implementations to lower onboarding friction
